rationale: C11 is the immediately preceding same-series Iran emergency report and supplies both the child’s overall five-part structure and extensive near-verbatim language. The child updates C11’s regulatory status, Tribunal award totals and account balances, Cases A/28 and A/29, government claims and settlement payments, private claims, and the identical concluding justification. C05 and C04 are earlier iterations of the same recurring template, but C11 is materially closer in wording, organization, and continuing matters.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I hereby report to the Congress on developments since the last Presidential report of May 13, 1998, concerning the national emergency with respect to Iran that was declared in [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of November 14, 1979. This report is submitted pursuant to section 204(c) of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, 50 U.S.C. 1703(c)(IEEPA).
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I hereby report to the Congress on developments since the last Presidential report of May 13, 1997, concerning the national emergency with respect to Iran that was declared in [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of November 14, 1979. This report is submitted pursuant to section 204(c) of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, 50 U.S.C. 1703(c) (IEEPA).
shared_material.explanation: The opening reporting formula is nearly verbatim, with only the prior-report date updated.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Iran-United States Claims Tribunal (the "Tribunal"), established at The Hague pursuant to the Algiers Accords, continues to make progress in arbitrating the claims before it. Since the period covered in my last report, the Tribunal has rendered three awards. This brings the total number of awards rendered by the Tribunal to 588, the majority of which have been in favor of U.S. claimants.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Iran-United States Claims Tribunal (the "Tribunal"), established at The Hague pursuant to the Algiers Accords, continues to make progress in arbitrating the claims before it. Since the period covered in my last report, the Tribunal has rendered five awards. This brings the total number of awards rendered by the Tribunal to 584, the majority of which have been in favor of U.S. claimants.
shared_material.explanation: The child directly reuses the Tribunal-status paragraph while updating the number of new and cumulative awards.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Therefore, the United States continues to pursue Case No. A/28, filed in September 1993, to require Iran to meet its obligation under the Algiers Accords to replenish the Security Account. The United States also continues to pursue Case No. A/29 to require Iran to meet its obligation of timely payment of its equal share of advances for Tribunal expenses when directed to do so by the Tribunal.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The situation reviewed above continues to implicate important diplomatic, financial, and legal interests of the United States and its nationals and presents an unusual challenge to the national security and foreign policy of the United States. The Iranian Assets Control Regulations issued pursuant to [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] continue to play an important role in structuring our relationship with Iran and in enabling the United States to implement properly the Algiers Accords.
